newsitem.title: USA: Morton, Autoliv sign definitive pact.
newsitem.headline: Morton, Autoliv sign definitive pact.

text.p: Morton International Inc and Autoliv AB of Sweden said Monday they approved a definitive agreement to combine Morton's automotive safety products operation with Autoliv.
The deal is subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals.
The new company, Autoliv Inc, will have global sales of more than US$3 billion, 15,000 employees and extensive operations in the United States, Europe and Asia, the companies said.

"Based on discussions between both companies and with our customers, I believe the growth potential of Autoliv Inc is greater than for ASP (Morton's automotive safety products) or Autoliv AB alone," said Fred Musone, ASP president who will become chief executive officer of Autoliv Inc.

He added Autoliv will expand both companies' product positions worldwide, leveraging each firm's research, development and engineering efforts and delivering integrated safety systems to automotive customers.
The combination of the two companies will create a group with an extensive range of key components needed for total safety automotive systems, the companies said.

"Synergies are expected to materialize in several areas, including sales, purchasing, production and RD&E (research, development and engineering), and in the form of reduced capital expenditures," Gunnar Bark, former Autoliv AB president said in a statement.
Bark will become chairman of Autoliv Inc.

The transaction was first announced in late September. Autoliv AB shares may be exchanged on a one-for-one basis for an aggregate of 53.5 percent of the equity of the new company, or 55,000,000 Autoliv Inc shares.
Upon approval of the merger, Morton's shareholders will exchange their interest in ASP for 46.5 percent of Autoliv Inc, or about 47,803,738 shares of the new company.
